models.name: EmbeddingGemma 2
models.base_arch: Gemma-based embedding encoder; optional vision and audio encoders
models.params: 740M in full; text-only 270M (130M backbone + 140M embedding table); text+image 440M; text+audio 570M
models.commercial_notes: Apache 2.0, not gated on Hugging Face (checked 2026-10-20); the card asks deployments to follow the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy (card line 282, rev 914f7f89).
models.speed_note: Measured on the rig's CPU in float32, in process with sentence-transformers: 2.6 chunks a second over 11,525 chunks, against nomic-embed-text's 5.6 on a CPU-only Ollama. Ollama 0.40.4 on Windows refuses every library tag (MLX tensor builds), so on this rig it runs in process, not through Ollama.
models.summary: An open embedding model that maps text, code, images, video and audio into one 768-dimension space, truncatable to 512, 256 or 128 (re-normalise after cutting). It reads 8,192 tokens and takes short task prefixes (for example `task: search result | query: ...`, and `title: {t} | text: {c}` for documents). Run it in bfloat16 or float32, never float16: the model card says its activations exceed float16's range and it then returns NaN or silently degraded vectors. Model card (rev 914f7f89): MTEB multilingual v2 61.36, English v2 68.46, code v1 78.68 at 768d; at 256d, English v2 67.78 and code 76.18; EmbeddingGemma 1 scores 61.15 multilingual and 68.76 code. On the studio's own pre-registered benchmark (93 queries over offrig's 11,525-chunk corpus, both arms scored after offrig's int8 quantization) it beat nomic-embed-text by +0.112 dense nDCG@10, one-sided 95% lower bound +0.065 (code +0.174, prose +0.041), so offrig adopts it at 768d. The 256d cut lost 0.043 against 768 (lower bound -0.062) and failed its bar.
